module_title: Trees, Binary Search Trees (BST), and Graph Traversal
introduction: This level shifts to Non-Linear data structures where data is organized in hierarchies or network graphs. Examiners heavily test tree traversal outputs and graph search algorithms.

core_concepts.title: Binary Trees and Traversals
core_concepts.description:
A tree where every node can have a maximum of 2 children (Left and Right).
**Depth-First Traversals:**
1. **Inorder:** Left $\rightarrow$ Root $\rightarrow$ Right
2. **Preorder:** Root $\rightarrow$ Left $\rightarrow$ Right
3. **Postorder:** Left $\rightarrow$ Right $\rightarrow$ Root

core_concepts.title: Binary Search Tree (BST)
core_concepts.description:
A highly specialized binary tree adhering to strict mathematical properties: 
1. Every node in the Left Subtree is strictly LESS than the Root. 
2. Every node in the Right Subtree is strictly GREATER than the Root. 
Average search time is drastically reduced to $O(\log n)$.

core_concepts.title: Graph Traversal Algorithms
core_concepts.description:
A graph is a complex network of Vertices (Nodes) and Edges. 
1. **BFS (Breadth-First Search):** Explores the graph completely level-by-level (horizontally). It strictly uses a **Queue** to track nodes. 
2. **DFS (Depth-First Search):** Explores down a single branch to its maximum depth before backtracking. It strictly uses a **Stack** (or recursion) to track nodes.

important_entities.name: The Inorder Traversal Property
important_entities.significance: A fundamental theorem in computer science: If you perform an **Inorder Traversal** exactly on a valid Binary Search Tree (BST), the resulting output sequence will ALWAYS be in perfectly **sorted (Ascending) order**.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The Worst Case of a BST
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: The Biggest Exam Trap: Students assume searching a BST always takes $O(\log n)$. However, if you insert already sorted data (e.g., 10, 20, 30, 40) into a standard BST, it degrades into a single straight line (a Skewed Tree). In this Worst Case scenario, the search time degrades catastrophically to **$O(n)$**, making it no better than a linked list.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Never mix them up: BFS pairs with Queue (B-Q). DFS pairs with Stack (D-S).

exam_strategy_tips: A favorite GATE and SSC JE IT question: 'Which binary tree traversal perfectly mimics the evaluation of mathematical postfix expressions?' Answer: Postorder Traversal.
